To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the zero-modes are given by the following linear combination of two contributions: 1) a contribution that is proportional to the vector potentials of the caloron and the anticaloron, and 2) a contribution that can be expressed in terms of the caloron field strength, up to a constant of integration, which is determined by a boundary condition at infinity.

the fermionic zero-modes for the non-trivial holonium calorons are constructed by different linear combination of two terms, which are proportional to the vector and the field strength, and that these terms are the same as the ones for the trivial calorons.

the zero modes of the Dirach operator for the adjoint representation fermions in the background of a calorons are constructed by different linear combination of the zero modes of two contributions adding the total caloron.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1) the computation of the zero-mode wave function of a fermionic field in the adjoint of SU(2) coupled to a unit charge calorons; 2) the computation of a zero-mode wave function for a fermionic field coupled to a unit-charge caloron in the adjoint SU(3); 3) the computation of zero-modes of a fermionic adjoint field in the case of a calorons of non-trivial holonomies.
the study of the properties of zero-modes in the Dirac operator for non-trivial caloron configurations.
the construction of the zero-modes for a non-trivial gauge field on R 3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gluino zero-modes of calorons with non-trivial holonomies are given by the sum of a contribution of a holonomy-independent zero-mode of a calorons with trivial holonomy and a holonomy-dependent contribution.
the zero-modes for calorons with non-trivial holonomies are not unique, but depend on the choice of a basis in the space of caloron fields.
the zero-modes are not determined by the holonomy of the caloron alone, but rather by the full caloron field configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a semiclassical approach, the zero-modes of the gluino fields are given by the same formulae as the corresponding bosonic fields.
the zero- modes are constructed from the two independent solutions of the Dirac operator in the background of the two instantons.
the zero-modes can be obtained by a linear combination of the zero-modes of the two constituent instanton and the anti-instanton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gluino zero modes are not necessarily proportional to the caloron gauge field.

, in contrast to the case of calorons with vanishing holonomy, the gluino zero-modes do not have a simple form in the case of non-trivial holonomies, and the corresponding expressions are not known in the literature.
the zero-modes are determined by the holonomy of the caloron, which is the same for calorons of all charges.
